# AirHorizon

AirHorizon is an iPhone and iPad aviation utility that provides a real-time artificial horizon and flight-style head-up display. It can use the device's own sensors or receive live telemetry from X-Plane 11 and X-Plane 12 over a local network.

Official website: https://airhorizon.app/
App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id1532431166
Support: https://valnikodeveloper.github.io/support/?app=airhorizon
Privacy Policy: https://airhorizon.app/privacy.html
Terms of Service: https://airhorizon.app/terms-of-service.html

## Main capabilities

- Real-time pitch and roll artificial horizon.
- Heading tape with one-tap markers and off-screen marker cues.
- Ground-speed and altitude tapes.
- Flight director guidance in Director Mode when supported simulator data is available.
- Night-vision HUD palette and adjustable display contrast.
- Portrait and landscape layouts for iPhone and iPad.
- One-tap pitch and roll calibration for different device mounting angles.

## X-Plane integration

- Compatible with X-Plane 11 and X-Plane 12.
- Receives standard X-Plane DATA packets over UDP on local network port 49000.
- Does not require an X-Plane plugin or additional desktop software.
- Uses X-Plane data rows 3, 17, 20, and 108 for speed, attitude, altitude, and flight-director information.

## Standalone operation and privacy

- Motion sensors provide pitch and roll.
- Location services provide ground speed and a true-north heading reference.
- The device barometer provides altitude when available.
- Sensor data is processed on the device.
- No AirHorizon account is required.

## Availability

- Available for iPhone and iPad.
- Requires iOS 18.1 or iPadOS 18.1 or later.
- Free to download, with some display options available through an optional Pro upgrade.

## Safety

AirHorizon is a consumer application for flight simulation, training reference, and general interest. It is not a certified aviation instrument, is not approved for navigation or aircraft operation, and must not be used as a primary or backup attitude reference in a real aircraft.
